exposure: International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society (ISN/RPS) classes of LN
outcome: Maternal outcomes (hypertension, active disease, remission status, renal flare, pre-eclampsia, renal function, mortality, dialysis dependency)
Fetal outcomes (successful pregnancy, spontaneous abortion, stillbirth, perinatal death, intrauterine growth retardation)
cohort: 52 women with biopsy-proven lupus nephritis who conceived at least 6 months after diagnosis
finding: Maternal and fetal outcomes in pre-existing lupus nephritis were primarily dependent on disease activity at the time of conception, with no significant differences found in relation to International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society classes of lupus nephritis.
mod_finding: There were more vaginal deliveries than caesarean sections (58.92% vs. 41.07%).
